issues.claim: For the founder email: "Your careers page also shows a good deal of coordination work being hired for at once — inspection scheduling and proposal compliance."
issues.problem: Contradicted. The careers page I opened lists only the 8 + 2 + 4 hiring plan (entry-level engineers/scientists/inspectors, 2 experienced geotechnical/environmental engineers, 4 NICET II & III construction inspectors) and a link to PERM postings. It contains no mention of a Scheduling Coordinator or a Proposal Coordinator (searched the rendered page text for 'schedul', 'proposal', 'coordinat' — no matches). Those two roles appear on third-party job boards (LinkedIn, Mediabistro), not on distinct-esi.com/careers/. A founder reading this will see the claim is wrong about his own site.
issues.fix: Change to "Your public job postings also show coordination work being hired for at once — inspection scheduling and proposal compliance" (or "two newly posted coordinator roles"), and, if the careers page is named at all, restrict it to the 14-hire plan.

issues.problem: Not supported. The Clients page lists project owners that are NY and NJ agencies only (MTA CC, NYC DDC/EDC/DEP/DOT/SCA, NYCHA, DSNY, NJDOT, NJ Transit, NJ Turnpike, PANYNJ, DASNY, Metro North, LIRR, plus NJ counties/municipalities). No PA or CT public agency appears. The corporate summary says the firm serves public and private clients "throughout New Jersey, Pennsylvania and the New York Metropolitan area" with CT only as a satellite office; the home page says it handles civil engineering in four states. Four-state public-agency client coverage is therefore an overstatement.
issues.fix: Reword to "public-agency clients across New Jersey and New York, registered and DBE/MBE-certified in four states", or drop the four-state qualifier.

issues.problem: Contradicted by the cited Qualifications page. Prequalifications/registrations listed are NY (DASNY, NYC SCA), NJ (NJ DPMC, NJTA, NJ Schools Development Authority) and PA (PennDOT ECMS registration) — three states. Connecticut has business registration, DBE/MBE/SBE certification and a Certificate of Authorization, but no prequalification.
issues.fix: Say "prequalifications in three states and DBE/MBE certification in four" or simply "multi-state prequalifications".

issues.claim: "at $28.69/hour (customer-service median, NJ, 2025, x1.25 for benefits)" (all three impact paragraphs).
issues.problem: Misstated benchmark. O*NET/BLS 2025 for 43-4051.00 New Jersey gives a median of $22.95/hour ($47,740/year), not $28.69. $28.69 is the median after the 1.25 loading (22.95 x 1.25 = 28.69). The arithmetic in the impact lines is internally consistent with $28.69 as the loaded rate, but the parenthetical presents a loaded figure as the median, so anyone who checks the source sees a wrong number.
issues.fix: Write "at $22.95/hour (NJ median, customer service representatives, BLS May 2025) loaded to $28.69 with a 1.25 benefits factor"; the resulting dollar totals stay unchanged.

issues.claim: "inspection, hazmat and geotechnical requests share one inbox" (section 1, Now).
issues.problem: Presented as fact but only partly traceable: the contact page shows one generic form (six visible fields: name, email, phone, company, city, message) and a single info@ address, but form submission routing/notification recipients are not published anywhere I could see. "Share one inbox" is an inference.
issues.fix: Say "arrive through one form to one generic inbox" or flag it as an assumption, e.g. "all three arrive in the same queue".

issues.problem: Body (title through "Prepared from publicly available information...", excluding the For-the-founder block and Sources) is 464 words by count, a little over the ~450-word target.
issues.fix: Trim roughly 20 words — e.g. shorten the section 3 'Agent would' sentence and the closing "Why this works" bullets.

issues.problem: The LinkedIn URL redirects to an auth wall / sign-up screen for an anonymous visitor, so the cited page cannot be opened as a source; the duties are verifiable only through syndicated copies (BeBee, Sercanto).
issues.fix: The claim itself is sound, but add a publicly open mirror as a secondary citation (e.g. the BeBee copy) or note that the posting is on LinkedIn and may require sign-in.

issues.problem: The audit's ranges ($1,434-$2,869; $4,303-$6,455; $4,131-$6,885) are far below the analysis file's ($3,000-$6,000; $8,000-$20,000; $15,000-$45,000) because the audit uses a single wage basis and tighter assumptions. Not a factual error, but the two deliverables do not agree if sent together.
issues.fix: No change needed for accuracy; if both documents travel together, add one line in the audit noting it deliberately uses a conservative single benchmark.
